text: Toward the end of the fifth or sixth month. <break time="0.8s" /> While the plague raged most fiercely outside. <break time="0.8s" /> The prince gave a masked ball. <break time="0.8s" /> For his thousand friends. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a splendid party. <break time="0.8s" /> But first let me tell you. <break time="0.8s" /> About the seven rooms. <break time="0.8s" /> In which it was held. <break time="0.8s" /> In most palaces. <break time="0.8s" /> Such rooms form a long, straight line. <break time="0.8s" /> But here a guest could see. <break time="0.8s" /> Little more than one room at a time. <break time="0.8s" /> There was a sharp turn. <break time="0.8s" /> Every twenty or thirty yards. <break time="0.8s" /> And at each turn. <break time="0.8s" /> A new and strange view appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> Each room had tall windows. <break time="0.8s" /> Of colored glass. <break time="0.8s" /> And the color of the glass. <break time="0.8s" /> Matched the decorations of the room. <break time="0.8s" /> The first room, at the eastern end. <break time="0.8s" /> Was blue. <break time="0.8s" /> And the others were purple, green. <break time="0.8s" /> Orange, white, and violet. <break time="0.8s" /> There were no lamps in the rooms. <break time="0.8s" /> But a brazier. <break time="0.8s" /> A large metal bowl of fire. <break time="0.8s" /> Burned in the hallway. <break time="0.8s" /> Behind each window. <break time="0.8s" /> The seventh room. <break time="0.8s" /> At the far western end. <break time="0.8s" /> Was covered in black velvet. <break time="0.8s" /> But its windows were a deep red. <break time="0.8s" /> The color of blood. <break time="0.8s" /> The firelight shining through the red glass. <break time="0.8s" /> Looked so ghostly. <break time="0.8s" /> That few guests were brave enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To step inside. <break time="0.8s" /> It was in this black room. <break time="0.8s" /> That a gigantic clock of ebony. <break time="0.8s" /> Stood against the western wall.
